THE MISSING 'why negative values are not a bug' VIGNETTE NOW HAS ITS EVIDENCE, from bd-01KZYP5CXFSXFV6HS65Y99CT4X. Under a pure null with 20 features and 4 runs, 3000 replicates:

  52.4 percent of total estimates are below zero

and all four estimators sit within 1.2 standard errors of zero. That single figure is the entire argument: an unbiased estimator centred at zero must be negative about half the time, so truncating would bias every null voxel upward. The vignette that is missing needs one simulation and one sentence, and both now exist.

The same bead supplies the other two chunks that vignette wants: plant a purely univariate effect and coherent reads 1.006 against configuration 0.013; plant a zero-mean pattern and configuration reads 1.039 against coherent 0.0008. Both recover the planted magnitude. So the abstract part of the framework - what coherent and configuration actually MEAN - becomes three short runnable examples rather than a paragraph the reader has to trust.
